tagline: The Andaman's duty-free archipelago — and Malaysia's cross-border gateway to Thailand.
summary: Langkawi is a 99-island duty-free destination on Malaysia's Andaman coast, anchored by luxury resorts (The Datai, Four Seasons, St Regis, Ritz-Carlton) and UNESCO geoparks. It is the natural Malaysian hub of the Andaman cross-border corridor — to Koh Lipe and Tarutao just north, and onward to Phuket — yet that crossing today is a slow, seasonal ferry.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Intra-Langkawi circuits (Kuah–Telaga–Datai–Kilim) and the Langkawi↔Koh Lipe/Tarutao crossing all sit inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The Langkawi↔Phuket Andaman leg (~140 nm) and onward to Banda Aceh/Sabang are Quanta-LR hybrid corridors — long-range, no charging dependency.

competitive_landscape: Conventional ferries (Langkawi–Penang, Langkawi–Kuala Perlis/Kedah) and seasonal Thai-border boats serve the area. The Andaman cross-border to Phuket is slow and seasonal — a structural gap Quanta-LR fills. Luxury guests today rely on private charter or transfers.
seasonality: The SW monsoon (roughly Apr–Oct) brings the Andaman's rougher conditions; the Langkawi–Koh Lipe ferry runs mainly Oct–May. Foiling extends the operable window and Quanta-LR range gives routing flexibility across monsoon windows.
regulatory_note: Cross-border to Thailand touches Malaysian and Thai maritime/immigration at established CIQ jetties (Telaga, Koh Lipe). Domestic circuits sit under Malaysian Marine Department oversight.
signature_routes: Kuah ↔ Telaga ↔ Datai Bay ↔ Kilim geoparks (intra-island)

grab.note: Phuket's Andaman cross-border partner: Langkawi closes the Phuket↔Langkawi corridor in the Grab phase-3 island-cluster network.
